choices.misconception: I evaluated $4^2$ as $4 \cdot 2 = 8$, so I got $18 - 4 + 8 = 22$.
I worked strictly left to right from the start, doing $18 - 6 = 12$ first, then $12 \div 3 \cdot 2 = 8$ and $8 + 16 = 24$.
I did the multiplication before the division, so $6 \div (3 \cdot 2) = 1$ and $18 - 1 + 16 = 33$.

hints: Exponents come first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.
Multiplication and division have equal rank, so do them from left to right: $6 \div 3$ comes before $\cdot 2$.

solutions.reliable: Start with the exponent: $4^2 = 16$. Next do multiplication and division from left to right: $6 \div 3 = 2$, then $2 \cdot 2 = 4$. The expression is now $18 - 4 + 16$, and working left to right gives $14 + 16 = 30$.
